bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you are a registered nurse in New South Wales, understanding your **registered nurse salary NSW hourly rate** is the first step to working out your annual, fortnightly and after-tax income. The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working the standard 38-hour week, the calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you 1,976 hours per year. For example, an hourly rate of $50.00 produces an annual gross salary of $98,800. If you work part-time, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and instantly see the annual, fortnightly and weekly figures.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a 38-hour week, that is your hourly rate × 76. Using the same $50.00 rate, your fortnightly gross would be $3,800. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

It is important to distinguish the **National Minimum Wage** from award rates. The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most registered nurses are covered by the **Nurses Award 2020** (or an enterprise agreement), which sets higher minimum rates. The award rate for a registered nurse depends on classification and experience. You can check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) on this site.

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a **casual loading** of 25% on top of the base hourly rate. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is therefore $33.05 per hour (including loading). On the [the timesheet](/), you can tick a checkbox to add the 25% casual loading automatically. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – always enter your base rate and let the tool add the loading.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional payment your employer makes into your super fund. It is calculated as 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 2026–27) and is paid **on top** of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. For a registered nurse earning $50.00 per hour, the super contribution would be $6.00 per hour, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means your total employment cost is higher than your gross pay. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Above that, you pay:
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more detail. Remember that this estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Average weekly earnings vary across states. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in **New South Wales** were $2,108.80 per week. That equates to an hourly rate of approximately $55.49 for a 38-hour week. This is a **state average** for all full-time employees, not a median for registered nurses. The national average for full-time adult ordinary time earnings was $2,083.70 per week. These figures can help you benchmark your own rate, but your actual pay should be based on your award or agreement.

For a registered nurse salary NSW hourly rate, the state average provides a useful reference, but individual rates depend on classification, experience, and whether you work in the public or private sector. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [reference tables](/data) can help you find the correct minimum rate for your role.

## Using the Timesheet

The [the timesheet](/) is designed to make these calculations easy. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and select whether you are permanent or casual. The tool will show your weekly, fortnightly and annual gross pay. It also estimates tax and super. Remember that the annual figure assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
